body:
# the contributor audit: full-parity cap weights and the odd product


`candidate dfa3dccc4c816783`
and `candidate 9bd56c5f5923c55d`.
The full source proofs were read. The full-parity verifier was rerun and
passed all 842 exact compatibility, quota, response, and facet-payment
checks. Exact verification supplements the geometric proof and does not
replace its all-normal or positive-width arguments.

The four-base triangle/square family retains actual lattice-compatible
fibers, classifies all relevant outside quotas and positive-width active
directions, and uses a continuous level match to produce exactly the two
deepest source parities. Its uniquely balanced triangle menu assigns
less than three eighths to the sole direction capturing its assigned
endpoint fiber. This refutes the claimed whole-fiber weight payment even
after optimizing over all actual menus. Its isolatable opposite source
facet instead has efficiency 4t^2/(6t-1)>4/9. Thus neither total convex
field capacity nor OC is contradicted.

For the odd integer product of the thin-edge d=4 family, strict equality
in the paired-tail bound and strict convexity of the proper quartic own
tail force the additional base tilt to vanish. The remaining active
caps and menus are precisely the repeated original family. Restricting
a full physical convex field to each fixed new integer coordinate and
summing preserves the prior obstruction, including normal dependence.
There are fifteen fibers and none has at least one quarter of the mass,
but only one of four ambient source parities is used. This rules out the
heavy-fiber premise as a repair, not a parity-sensitive global theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
